description: Naturally occurring organic acid found in citrus fruits. Used to regulate acidity, enhance flavor, and act as an antioxidant in beverages, preserves, and processed foods.
health_effects: Generally Recognized As Safe (GRAS) by global authorities.
May cause minor teeth enamel erosion if consumed in excessive concentrated amounts.
max_daily_intake_note: Not limited under standard dietary guidelines.

description: Extracted from edible red seaweeds. Used widely to gel, thicken, and stabilize food products like dairy, jellies, and plant-based milks.
health_effects: Food-grade refined carrageenan is approved for human consumption.
Some individuals report gastrointestinal sensitivity or bloating with high intake.
max_daily_intake_note: ADI is established at up to 75 mg/kg body weight per day.

description: Chemical preservative commonly used in acidic foods such as fruit juices, jellies, carbonated drinks, and condiments to inhibit growth of mold, yeast, and bacteria.
health_effects: When combined with Vitamin C (Ascorbic Acid) under heat/light, small amounts of benzene can form.
May cause mild hypersensitivity reactions in asthmatic individuals.
max_daily_intake_note: Acceptable Daily Intake (ADI) is 0 to 5 mg/kg body weight.

description: Synthetic lemon yellow azo dye used in jellies, confectionery, soft drinks, and snacks.
health_effects: Associated with hyperactivity symptoms in sensitive children.
Can trigger allergic reactions or hives in people sensitive to aspirin.

description: Synthetic blue dye used in jellies, beverages, baked goods, and syrups.
Sodium salt of glutamic acid, providing umami savory flavor in noodles, soups, and savory snacks.
health_effects: Deemed safe by FDA and EFSA.
Transient sensitivity (headache, flushing) reported in sensitive consumers when consumed in very high doses without food.
max_daily_intake_note: ADI not specified (consumed at customary dietary levels).
